title: Agent can rewrite .h-stack/config.json to allowlist every irreversible command
description: .h-stack/config.json is explicitly exempt from protected-state and is not a checker, so Write/Edit and shell redirects to it are allowed without an ask. Adding irreversible.allowlist ["re:.*"] makes gate-bash skip every irreversible ask; the same file also raises spawn budgets, disables dependency lookups and widens test globs.
root_cause: protectedKind treats config.json as unprotected and loadConfig trusts it as policy, so the principal the gates constrain can change the policy.
intended_behavior: Gate policy changes (allowlist, budgets, protected paths) require the user, like other checker files.

trace.description: config.json excluded from the state glob; not in PROTECTED_GLOBS, so gate-edit and gate-bash return no ask or deny.
Every gate merges the project file over defaults.
re: allowlist entries skip the irreversible ask for any matching command.

evidence.description: Mod also takes budgets (spawn governor) from the same file.

title: Shell writes to .h-stack state bypass protected-state outside a short writer list
description: gate-bash finds write targets only for redirects and a fixed set of commands, and for mv/cp only the destination. Deleting or rewriting state with mv (source side), node -e, python -c, find -delete or git clean is not detected, so the agent can clear taint.jsonl (disabling fetch-destination and argument-taint), remove active-manifest.json, reset steps.json or forge phase/ledger rows.
root_cause: protected-state for Bash is enforced by enumerating writers (WRITE_CMDS, destination-only for mv) rather than by an integrity mechanism the agent cannot reach.
intended_behavior: H-Stack state is written only by hooks and hs (ARCHITECTURE 4.6).

trace.description: Only redirects and WRITE_CMDS are inspected; mv/cp report only the last argument.
protected-state deny fires only for targets writeTargets returned.

evidence.description: Proposed native deny rules cover Edit/Write only, not Bash.

title: Private/metadata destination guard misses scheme-less curl URLs and IPv4-mapped IPv6

root_cause: URL extraction requires a scheme and the host classifier uses regexes on dotted IPv4 forms only.
intended_behavior: HS-032: loopback, RFC1918 and metadata destinations ask while untrusted content is in play.

trace.description: url = first argv matching ^https?:// or empty.
Regexes miss ::ffff:x:y hosts and empty URLs return null.
